decisionTitle: cli.test.js already existed from task 14 with 12 of 13 required scenarios; added only the missing no-network-require check
rationale: roman-numerals/cli.js and roman-numerals/test/cli.test.js were already present and implemented (task 14 delivered both, per handoff/reports/report_14.json, even though task 14's own filesToEdit only listed cli.js). The existing cli.test.js already covered scenarios 1-10 from this task's description (success --number, success --roman, --help, both flags together, out-of-range number in both directions, invalid roman numeral, stdin-as-number, stdin-as-roman, missing-input via TTY-like no-stdin and via whitespace-only stdin, and --out writing to a temp file with cleanup), all via child_process.spawnSync against the built cli.js binary (no require() of cli.js). The one gap was scenario 11: an automated check that cli.js and lib.js contain no require() of networking modules (http, https, net, dgram, dns, plus http2/tls for good measure). I added a single new test that reads both source files and regex-checks for require('<module>') calls for that module list, without touching cli.js/lib.js or the test runner config (still plain `node --test` per package.json). Ran `cd roman-numerals && npm test`: 24/24 passing (23 pre-existing + 1 new).
ignoredContext: handoff/RESEARCH.md describes an unrelated project (tekstovyy-kvest / lib/state-machine.js) and does not reflect the actual roman-numerals directory in this workspace; it was disregarded in favor of reading the real files on disk.
